sections.label: Changi Airport passenger decline
sections.summary: Singapore did the same on 24 March this year, and Changi Airport now has fewer passengers than when Terminal 1 opened in 1981.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singapore did the same on 24 March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, we have fewer passengers than when we first opened Changi Airport Terminal 1 in 1981 – we have gone back more than 40 years because of COVID-19.

sections.label: Changi passenger and flight volumes
sections.summary: Compared to pre-COVID-19, Changi Airport serves 1.5% of usual passenger volume and 6% of usual passenger flights.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Compared to pre-COVID-19, Changi Airport is serving 1.5% of our usual passenger volume; and 6% of the usual number of passenger flights.

sections.label: Cargo flights and direct cities
sections.summary: More than two and a half times more cargo flights now partially offset fewer passenger flights, with direct flights to 49 cities versus 160 pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is because we are flying more than two and a half times more cargo flights now, which partially offsets the reduction in passenger flights; so all the online buying of goods has contributed to cargo and allowed us to mount more cargo flights.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We now have direct flights to 49 cities in the world, compared to pre-COVID-19, 160.

sections.label: Jobs rationalised in aviation
sections.summary: One thousand nine hundred jobs have been rationalised through open vacancies not filled, early retirement and voluntary release scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One thousand nine hundred jobs have been rationalised through open vacancies that were not filled, early retirement and voluntary release scheme.

sections.label: Two-year pause and support
sections.summary: A two-year pause was decided for clarity on air travel recovery, with Jobs Support Scheme, Enhanced Aviation Support Package and temporary redeployment programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Given the current situation, we have decided to take a two-year pause, so that we have more clarity on the pace of air travel recovery, before deciding how to proceed with the project.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This includes the Jobs Support Scheme, where the aviation sector benefits from the highest level of support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have also provided cost relief through the Enhanced Aviation Support Package and temporary redeployment programmes for workers affected.

sections.label: Daily PCR testing capacity
sections.summary: More than 27,000 individuals are tested daily, up from 2,000 in March, using PCR tests, with capacity on track for 40,000 tests a day by November 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, we test more than 27,000 individuals daily – from 2,000 in March, to now, 27,000 daily today – using diagnostic polymerase chain reaction, or PCR, tests and we are on track to increase our testing capacity to 40,000 tests a day by November 2020.

sections.label: Testing replacing Stay-Home Notice
sections.summary: Some increased capacity will be allocated to test air passengers, allowing borders to open selectively by replacing Stay-Home Notice with tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Part of this increased capacity will be allocated to test air passengers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In other words, on a selective basis, we can open up our border, do away with Stay-Home Notice, or SHN, which is a big deterrent to travel for anybody and replace SHN with tests.

sections.label: Changi Airport testing capacity
sections.summary: Changi Airport has set up a facility to swab up to 10,000 passengers a day and plans a dedicated COVID-19 testing laboratory.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Changi Airport has already set up a facility to swab up to 10,000 passengers a day as a start and with some notice, it can ramp up the numbers quite readily.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the next few months, we plan to set up at Changi Airport a dedicated COVID-19 testing laboratory to support aviation recovery.

sections.label: Dubai and Istanbul air hubs
sections.summary: Air hubs Dubai in the United Arab Emirates and Istanbul in Turkey restored flights quickly and are at about 30% of pre-COVID-19 volumes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Air hubs such as Dubai in the United Arab Emirates and Istanbul in Turkey have restored flights quite quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Now, they are at about 30% of pre-COVID-19 volumes.

sections.label: MFA arrangements with five countries
sections.summary: MFA led the inter-agency effort and concluded arrangements with Brunei, China, Japan, Malaysia and the Republic of Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MFA has led this inter-agency effort and concluded arrangements with Brunei, China, Japan, Malaysia and the Republic of Korea.

sections.label: Transfer passengers through Singapore
sections.summary: Since June about 27,000 passengers transferred safely through Singapore, now about 2,500 weekly, with numbers expected to rise steadily.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since June, about 27,000 passengers transferred safely through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On a weekly basis, we are now serving about 2,500 transfer passengers and we expect the numbers to rise steadily.

sections.label: Opening up to more countries
sections.summary: No lengthy bilateral negotiations are needed; Singapore opened up to Brunei and New Zealand, then Australia ex-Victoria and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There is no need for lengthy bilateral negotiations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We opened up to travellers from Brunei and New Zealand last month, and more recently – in fact, last week – we opened up to Australia, ex-Victoria, and Vietnam.

sections.label: UK travel advisory and entry
sections.summary: A travel advisory remains against Singaporean residents travelling to the UK, and travellers from the UK cannot enter Singapore freely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At present, UK's incidence rate is quite high, so we still have a travel advisory against Singaporean residents travelling to the UK and we are also not ready to allow travellers from the UK to enter freely into Singapore.

sections.label: Air Travel Bubbles with safe countries
sections.summary: For safe countries or regions, Singapore will negotiate Air Travel Bubbles or pursue such ATBs with them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The fourth thing we will do, for these safe countries or regions, is that we will also negotiate Air Travel Bubbles or ATBs, or pursue such ATBs with them.

sections.label: ATB risk management and Hong Kong
sections.summary: ATBs will be set only with safe countries and regions, with daily traveller quotas and COVID-19 test protocols; Hong Kong announced ATB intentions including Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: While we should establish ATBs only with safe countries and regions, we can further manage risks by setting a quota on the number of travellers per day and ensuring that everyone abides by a COVID-19 test protocols.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hong Kong has publicly announced its intention to establish ATBs with several countries, including Singapore, and we have responded positively.

sections.label: Replacing 14-day SHN
sections.summary: The 14-day SHN in a hotel could be replaced by a more stringent and repeated test protocol, which will be studied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, we can replace the 14-day SHN in a hotel with new requirements, such as a more stringent and repeated test protocol – on arrival, three days later, five days later, seven days later, we will study that.

sections.label: Singapore re-opening its borders
sections.summary: The message to the world is that Singapore has started to re-open its borders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The message we want to send to the world is this – Singapore has started to re-open its borders.

sections.label: Stakes for Singapore
sections.summary: At stake are hundreds of thousands of jobs, Singapore's status as an air hub, its relevance to the world, economic survival and ability to determine its own future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: What is at stake is not just hundreds of thousands of jobs, but our status as an air hub, Singapore's relevance to the world, our economic survival, and in turn, our ability to determine our own future.

sections.label: ASEAN travel and cargo reopening
sections.summary: Singapore takes a country-by-country approach to reopening, with unilateral openings and Reciprocal Green Lanes, and cargo flights are 2.5 times more than COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of now, I would not say ASEAN is ready to discuss a regional plan but individual countries, member states, are doing our own assessment of what is safe, what is unsafe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Within ASEAN countries, as Members know, we have opened up to Vietnam, it has a very good track record and MOH recognises that, so we can have opened up unilaterally for Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Where possible, and we have RGLs or Reciprocal Green Lane arrangements such as with Malaysia or Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we will push in that direction, taking a country-by-country approach and bearing in mind ASEAN is an important market for us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On cargo, yes, we will ramp up when there is demand and when demand justifies it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Therefore, today, because of the ramping up, cargo flights is 2.5 times more than COVID-19.

sections.label: Retaining Singapore air hub status
sections.summary: Making the first moves now means Singapore can stay ahead and retain its air hub status when a vaccine arrives and air travel reopens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If we succeed, if we can make the first moves, then when there is a vaccine, when air travel opens again internationally, we will find that Singapore is right up there, ahead of the curve and we can retain our air hub status.

sections.label: SIA recapitalisation and environmental tax
sections.summary: SIA is ferrying 1.5% of its passenger volume and would have gone under without recapitalisation, so now is not the time for an environmental tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SIA, as I mentioned, is ferrying 1.5% of its passenger volume, so it is not about passing the costs to passengers; it is that there are no passengers to pass the costs to now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Because if you understand how a company is run – when a company runs out of cash, it is insolvent, it goes under.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And SIA would have gone under if not for the massive recapitalisation exercise that happened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It itself is trying to generate as much revenue as it can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, this is really not the time now to talk about an environmental tax on SIA.

sections.label: Passenger demand despite testing costs
sections.summary: Testing brings extra segregation and higher costs, but many passengers will pay more and be tested to travel, and demand exists because supply has been decimated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you have to do a test, you have to have extra segregation and all that, cost is higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, there are many passengers who are still prepared to pay a bit more, even go through the discomfort of being tested in order to travel, either for business, leisure or just visit relatives and other reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think the demand is there because the supply has totally been decimated.

sections.label: Opening borders and reviving air travel
sections.summary: Singapore is taking active steps to open borders and revive air travel, and is in contact with an airline industry keen to return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And we are taking active steps, as I had mentioned, to open up our borders and revive air travel again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are in contact with the airline industry; many are still very keen to come back to Singapore.

sections.label: Small size as key reason
sections.summary: The key reason is the fact that Singapore is small.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The key reason is the fact that we are small.

sections.label: Testing on arrival for travellers
sections.summary: Travellers from Brunei, New Zealand, Vietnam and Australia, opened up to unilaterally, must be tested upon arrival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For travellers that we open up to unilaterally, they have to be tested upon arrival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For travellers that we open up unilaterally to – travellers from Brunei, New Zealand, Vietnam, Australia – they will be tested upon arrival.

sections.label: Reason for SHN requirement
sections.summary: Travellers requiring SHN or SHN Plus do so because of the incubation period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Just to elaborate on Minister Ong's explanation, for travellers who come in that require SHN or SHN Plus, the reason they require SHN or SHN Plus is because of the incubation period.

sections.label: Zero days SHN for four countries
sections.summary: Brunei, New Zealand, Vietnam and Australia, excluding Victoria, require zero days of SHN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In the case of Brunei, New Zealand, Vietnam and Australia, ex Victoria, we require zero days of SHN.

sections.label: Airlines resuming flights assessment
sections.summary: They are listening to the Statement, make their own assessment on flights to resume, and announced resuming up to 15% of flights by year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I am sure they are listening to the Statement and they make their own assessment what are the flights they want to resume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They have announced they will resume up to 15% of their flights by the end of this year.

sections.label: Enhanced Aviation Support Package for SIA
sections.summary: The March Resilience Budget included a $350 million Enhanced Aviation Support Package to help SIA maintain its Minimum Connection Network and mount cargo flights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Also, from the Government's perspective, you will recall in March, Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Resilience Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And that includes the $350 million Enhanced Aviation Support Package and part of that package is to help SIA maintain this Minimum Connection Network because Singaporeans do need to go in and out – students, families and so on – and allow Singaporeans from overseas to come home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, even though load factor is low, we support SIA to continue these flights and also to mount cargo flights so that our supply chain is not affected.

sections.label: SIA investment in new aircraft
sections.summary: SIA invested heavily in new aircraft like the A350s and 787 Dreamliner, which contribute about 25% less CO2 emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As for the environmental tax that was mooted earlier, I just want to declare that SIA has invested very heavily on new aircraft, such as the A350s and the 787 Dreamliner that by itself, contribute about 25% less CO2 emissions and the fuel consumption is only three to four litres per hundred kilometre travel of passengers.

sections.label: Fees waived for CAG SIA
sections.summary: CAG, SIA, CAAS and MOT will work closely together, and some fees and charges have been waived for this period to reduce costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: CAG, SIA, CAAS and MOT will work closely together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I do not have the details but some of the fees and charges have been waived for this period in order to reduce costs.
